newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rupee closes at 35.89/90 on RBI dlr buying.
newsitem.headline: Indian rupee closes at 35.89/90 on RBI dlr buying.

text.p: The Indian rupee closed at 35.89/90 against the dollar on Friday compared to the opening level of 35.88/89, dealers said.
Dealers said the rupee closed mildly lower on dollar purchases by an influential Calcutta-based state bank and the Reserve Bank of India (RBI).
The Calcutta bank bought at 35.90 earlier in the day. The RBI came in towards the close, buying up dollars from all those who chose to sell at 35.8950 level, dealers said.
"They should have bought substantial amounts today," said a dealer, referring to the central bank which has been regularly intervening in the market to prevent a fall in dollar's value.
"Buying interest from them (RBI, the Calcutta bank and companies) would continue to come in at these levels," said a foreign bank in its forex commentary.
"Stay long and await some action towards the month-end when 35.95/96 levels should be tested again," it said. The rupee touched a low of 35.98 in the first half of February.
Dealers said the exchange rate reflected a slowdown in Indian imports and possibly a postponement of overseas remittances. The usual pre-budget spurt in dollar demand is missing this year, they said.
India's budget is to be unveiled on February 28.
Some dealers expect the rupee to inch closer to 36 rupees per dollar level by March-end on the back of likely steps to rejuvenate industrial output and increase imports.
The forward premia inched up on Friday as the RBI stayed away. "There was also genuine paying on account of FCNR (foreign currency non-resident account held by expatriate Indians)," said a dealer.
The six month annualised premium closed at 7.13 percent compared to the previous close of 6.97 percent, dealers said.
